name: Gorkha
summary: Historic hilltop town and birthplace of King Prithvi Narayan Shah, who unified Nepal in the 18th century. The Gorkha Durbar (palace) complex combines royal palace, fort, and temple architecture atop a hill overlooking the Trisuli Valley, with panoramic views of Manaslu, Himalchuli, Ganesh Himal, and the Annapurna range. A UNESCO-recognized heritage site, rebuilt after damage in the 2015 earthquake.

best_time_to_visit.primary: October to May (aligns with Nepal's main trekking season); spring (March-May) and autumn (September-November) specifically recommended
best_time_to_visit.notes: June to September is hot, humid, and monsoon clouds obscure mountain views.

transport_options: Regular buses and private vehicles from Kathmandu to Gorkha Bazaar (approx 5-6 hours)
Also reachable via Abu Khaireni on the Kathmandu-Pokhara highway route
route_from_kathmandu.within_gorkha: From Gorkha Bazaar, climb approx 1,500-1,700 stone steps (30-45 minutes) to reach Gorkha Durbar, or take a taxi/jeep via an alternate road to a shorter, less strenuous route

difficulty_level: Easy to moderate (steep stair climb to the palace, but no trekking gear needed)
time_required: Day trip, or overnight for a more relaxed visit including sunrise views
things_to_do: Explore Gorkha Durbar palace complex and Gorkha Durbar Museum
Visit the 17th-century Kalika Temple within the durbar grounds
Watch sunrise over the Himalayas from the palace hilltop
Try local dal bhat and other Nepali street food
practical_notes: Gorkha Durbar site is generally open daily (commonly cited hours around 9am-5pm), with affordable entry fees for both domestic and international visitors. Hiring a local guide is optional but adds historical context.
culture_notes: The site holds deep spiritual significance for Nepalis as the birthplace of unified Nepal; animal sacrifices to the goddess Kali still take place at the temple on significant lunar dates.
